Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool designed to help us understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to identify any potential concerns or symptoms that may be affecting your daily life and overall mental health.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and held in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to judge. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your feelings and experiences over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and natural as possible.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. It's simply a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional well-being during this significant life transition. Are you ready to get started? Let's begin with the first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Yeah... I think so. I mean, it's been a bit of a challenge lately. With the baby, I'm just so tired all the time. But, there have been moments when my husband does something silly or the baby makes a cute face, and I do laugh. It's just not as often as it used to be, I guess. I feel like I'm just going through the motions a lot of the time, trying to keep up with feedings and changing diapers. But, when I do laugh, it feels really good. It's like a little break from all the stress and worry I've been feeling about the baby's health and whether I'm doing everything right. So, to answer your question, I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but it's not as easy as it used to be.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I'm glad you acknowledged that. It feels like you understand where I'm coming from. To be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle to find the humor in things lately. I mean, when you're running on fumes and worried about your baby's every sneeze, it's hard to see the funny side of things. But, like I said, there are moments when my husband or the baby does something that makes me laugh, and it's like a weight lifts off my shoulders for a second. It's just...it's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm living in a constant state of "what if" - what if the baby gets sick, what if I'm not doing enough, what if...and it's exhausting. But, yeah, I do laugh sometimes, and it's nice to feel like myself for a little bit.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'm just so tired all the time, and it's hard to think about anything beyond the next feeding or diaper change. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying things. But, there are some things that I do look forward to, like my husband coming home from work and helping out with the baby, or taking a warm shower by myself. Those things sound really small, but they feel like luxuries to me right now. And, I guess, I do look forward to seeing the baby smile or laugh - that's always a highlight of my day. But, overall, I'd say I'm not really looking forward to things like I used to, and that's been kind of sad for me. I feel like I've lost a little bit of myself in all of this, and I'm not sure how to get it back.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I'd say that's happened a few times. I mean, when the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, or when I'm not producing enough milk, or when I just feel like I'm not doing everything right... I do tend to blame myself. I think to myself, "If only I had done this or that, things would be better." It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to feel like I'm somehow failing as a mother. And, sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me and tell me that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of self-doubt. I'll think, "No, I should be doing more, I should be better at this." It's like, I'm my own worst critic, and it's exhausting. But, at the same time, I'm trying to be kinder to myself and remind myself that I'm doing the best I can, and that it's okay to make mistakes. It's just... it's hard, you know.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? What if she's not developing like she should be? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get really anxious. And, sometimes, it's not even about anything specific - I'll just feel this general sense of unease, like something is off, but I don't know what it is. It's really frustrating, because I know it's not rational, but I just can't seem to shake it off. And, it's hard to explain to my husband, because he's always like, "What's wrong?" And, I'm like, "I don't know, I just feel anxious." It's like, I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop, or something. But, at the same time, when I do talk to him about it, he's really supportive, and he tries to reassure me that everything is okay. So, that helps a bit. But, yeah, the anxiety has been really tough to deal with.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

.. that's happened to me a few times, especially at night when the house is quiet and I'm just sitting there with the baby. I'll be feeding her or rocking her to sleep, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. It's like, my heart starts racing and my mind starts racing, and I feel like I'm going to lose control or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong - like, what if the baby stops breathing, or what if there's a fire in the house, or what if... and it just spirals out of control. It's like, I know it's irrational, but I just can't seem to calm myself down. And, it's hard to explain to my husband, because he's always like, "What's wrong?" And, I'm like, "I don't know, I just feel scared." It's like, I'm waiting for something bad to happen, and it's just really overwhelming. But, when it happens, I try to take some deep breaths and remind myself that everything is okay, and that I'm safe, and that the baby is safe. And, sometimes, I'll get up and walk around the house, or I'll call my husband to come and sit with me, and that helps a bit. But, yeah, the panic has been really tough to deal with.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah... that's definitely been happening. I mean, taking care of a new baby is just so overwhelming, you know? It's like, I'm responsible for this tiny human's entire existence, and that's a lot of pressure. And, sometimes, it just feels like everything is piling up on me - the feedings, the diaper changes, the lack of sleep... it's just so much to handle. And, I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, you know? Like, I'm just trying to get through each day without losing my mind. And, sometimes, it feels like everything is just getting on top of me, and I don't know how to cope. I'll be sitting there, feeling okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. And, it's hard to explain to my husband, because he's trying to be supportive, but he doesn't really get it, you know? He's not the one who's up all night feeding the baby, or who's responsible for making sure the baby is okay all the time. So, sometimes I just feel like I'm shouldering all of this by myself, and it's really tough. But, at the same time, I know that I'm not alone, and that lots of other moms are going through the same thing. So, that helps a bit, I guess.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I mean, I'll be lying in bed, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries, and I'll feel really unhappy and overwhelmed. And, it's hard to fall asleep when you're feeling like that. I'll just lie there, staring at the ceiling, and thinking about all the things that are stressing me out. And, even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night and have trouble getting back to sleep. It's like, my brain just won't shut off, you know? And, it's not just the baby waking me up that's the problem - although, that's definitely part of it. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm always "on" now, and I never get a break. Even when I'm sleeping, I'm still listening for the baby, and waiting for her to wake up and need me again. So, it's hard to really relax and get a good night's sleep. And, when I don't get enough sleep, it just makes everything else harder, you know? It's like, I'm already feeling overwhelmed and unhappy, and then I'm tired on top of it, and it's just... it's a really tough cycle to break.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah... I'd say that's happened to me a few times since having the baby. I mean, it's not all the time, but there are definitely days when I just feel really down and sad. It's like, I'll be sitting there, looking at the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. Or, I'll be thinking about how hard this all is, and how I'm not doing a good enough job, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm sad all the time, or that I don't love my baby. It's just... I don't know, it's like I'm grieving the life I had before, or something. Like, I'm grieving the freedom to just get up and go whenever I want, or to be able to take a shower without worrying about who's going to watch the baby. It's like, I know I'm supposed to be happy and grateful for this new life, but sometimes it just feels really overwhelming and sad. And, it's hard to talk to my husband about it, because he's just so happy and excited to be a dad, and I don't want to ruin that for him. So, I just kind of... I don't know, I just try to push through it, I guess. But, it's nice to finally be talking to someone about it, because it feels like maybe I'm not just crazy or something.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... that's happened to me a few times. I'd say it's not every day, but there have been days when I've just broken down and cried. It's like, everything just becomes too much, and I feel so overwhelmed and sad, and I just can't hold it in anymore. Sometimes it's when I'm feeling really tired and frustrated, and the baby is crying, and I just feel like I'm at my breaking point. Other times, it's when I'm thinking about how hard this all is, and how I'm not doing a good enough job, and I just feel like I'm failing somehow. It's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm crying all the time, or that I'm not happy to be a mom. It's just... I don't know, it's like my emotions are just really close to the surface right now, and sometimes they just spill over. And, it's funny, because sometimes I'll be crying, and my husband will be like, "What's wrong?" And, I'll be like, "I don't know, I just am." Because, it's not like there's one specific thing that's wrong, it's just... everything, I guess. But, yeah, the crying has happened a few times, and it's just... it's nice to finally be talking to someone about it, I guess. It feels like maybe I'm not just losing my mind or something.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think that's ever occurred to me. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad at times, but I don't think I've ever had thoughts of harming myself. I think I've just felt more like, "I don't know how I'm going to get through this," or "I'm not doing a good enough job," but it's never gone to a place where I've thought about harming myself. I think I've just been more focused on trying to survive each day and take care of my baby, even when it feels really hard. And, I've had a lot of support from my husband and family, which has helped a lot. So, no, I don't think that's something I've ever considered.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns following the birth of their baby, including feelings of sadness, overwhelm, and anxiety. They report difficulty coping with the demands of caring for a new baby and express feelings of worthlessness and guilt related to perceived inadequacies as a mother. The patient's symptoms and concerns suggest a need for further evaluation and support to address potential postpartum depression or anxiety.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 20, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient mentions that it's been a struggle to find humor in things lately and feels like they're living in a constant state of worry, but also shares that there are moments when they do laugh, indicating a significant decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things.</sym>, <sym>Patient states they don't look forward to things as much as they used to, citing exhaustion and feeling like they're just trying to survive, but still mentions a few things they look forward to, aligning with 'Definitely less than I used to</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to blaming themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong, citing specific situations and thoughts that align with self-blame, but also mentions trying to be kinder to themselves, indicating it happens 'some of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports feeling scared or panicky for no very good reason, especially at night, and describes a wave of panic washing over them, indicating that this happens sometimes, but not constantly.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with the responsibilities of caring for a new baby, but also mentions that they are trying to get through each day and that knowing other moms are going through the same thing helps a bit, which suggests they are not completely unable to cope.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>The patient reports feeling sad and down several times since having the baby, describing it as a wave of sadness that washes over them, indicating that this feeling occurs quite often.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports crying 'a few times' and feeling overwhelmed, indicating that they have been unhappy to the point of crying more than occasionally, but not most of the time.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 20 indicates a high possibility of depression, and the patient's reports of feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with the demands of caring for a new baby suggest a need for urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities, such as taking a warm bath or reading a book
3. Support patient in developing a sleep hygiene routine to improve sleep quality
4. Connect patient with local resources, such as support groups or online forums, for new mothers experiencing <med>postpartum depression</med> or <med>anxiety</med>
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
